raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week program summary, integrating strength (with spinal-sparing constraints), cardio twice weekly, abs work, anti-inflammatory nutrition, and sleep/recovery. It’s organized in three phases, 3 strength sessions/week (A/B/C), plus 2 cardio sessions and 2 short movement/recovery minis. All lifting avoids heavy axial loading and loaded spinal flexion; prioritize neutral spine and 360-degree bracing.

Global rules and cues
- No heavy spinal loading or loaded spinal flexion. Avoid back/front squats, heavy barbell deadlifts, good mornings, sit-ups/Crunch machines, heavy ab rollouts.
- Main implements: belt squat, goblet/DB, landmine, machines, hip thrusts, chest-supported rows, carries.
- RPE targets: Phase 1 = 6–7, Phase 2 = 7.5–8.5 (with intensity strategies), Phase 3 = 7–8 (quality), Week 12 testing uses specific peaking.
- Tempo: Early control 3-0-1-0, then mostly 2-0-1-0, with strategic pauses.
- Rest: 2–3 min compounds, 60–90 s accessories.
- Progression: Add 2.5–5% load or 1 rep/set if all reps clean. If any back signals, reduce load 10% and/or shorten ROM.
- Warm-up every session (8–10 min): 90/90 or croc breathing 4–6 slow breaths; cat-camel (unloaded), half-kneeling hip flexor, adductor rock-backs, ankle rocks, T-spine openers; activation (dead bug, clams/side-lying hip abduction, band pull-aparts/face pulls). Then 2–3 ramp sets on first two lifts.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and motor control; build patterns, core stiffness, unilateral strength. RPE 6–7.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength push; heavier via safe implements; top-set/back-off, pauses, limited clusters; deload Week 8. RPE 7.5–8.5.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation, controlled power, and Week 12 testing. RPE 7–8 except test lifts.

Weekly cardio (2x/week)
- Structure: Nonconsecutive days, ideally on non-lifting days or after A/C.
- Phase 1: Zone 2 base—start 20 min and build to 25 min; Week 4 deload 20–22 min.
- Phase 2: One Zone 2 (30–35 min) + one controlled interval day (e.g., bike 6–8 x 45–60 s @ RPE 7 with 60–90 s easy); Week 8 deload both Zone 2 at 22–25 min.
- Phase 3: Maintain one Zone 2 (30–36 min) + one interval day (sled/bike/elliptical); Week 12 taper to two Zone 2 20–25 min; avoid intervals within 48 h before lower-body tests.

Abs/core work (2–3x/week, 10–15 min; spine neutral)
- Phase 1: Dead bug 3x6–8/side; bird dog 3x6–8/side; side plank 3x20–30 s/side; Pallof press 3x10/side; light suitcase carry 3–4x20–30 m/side.
- Phase 2: Dead bug with band/ball 3x8/side; side plank with abduction 3x20–30 s; Pallof to step-out 3x8–10/side; stir-the-pot 3x8–12 each way; suitcase or farmer carry 4x30–45 m.
- Phase 3: Long-lever dead bug 3x8/side; hard-style plank 6–8 x 10–15 s on/10–15 s off; Copenhagen plank short-to-mid 3x15–25 s/side; heavy suitcase/offset carry 4–5x30–50 m.

Here’s a practical sleep and recovery protocol to run alongside the 12-week plan. It prioritizes spinal-friendly restoration, consistent routines, and simple tracking so you can adjust training if recovery dips.

Core sleep targets
- Sleep duration: 7.5–9 hours per night. Anchor a consistent bedtime/wake time within ±30 minutes, even on weekends.
- Sleep quality: fall asleep within 20–30 minutes, ≤1–2 brief awakenings, wake feeling reasonably refreshed 5+ days/week.

Daily sleep routine
- Daylight anchor: 5–10 minutes outdoor light within 30 minutes of waking; brief outdoor light again late afternoon.
- Caffeine: cap at 1–3 mg/kg total and finish ≥8 hours before bed.
- Alcohol: avoid within 3–4 hours pre-sleep; limit weekly intake overall.
- Naps: optional 10–20 minutes before 3 p.m. if sleep debt accumulates; avoid longer or late naps.
- Evening wind-down (60–75 minutes pre-bed):
  - Dim lights, reduce screens or use blue-light filters/night mode.
  - Light mobility 5–8 minutes: hip flexor stretch, 90/90 breathing, T-spine openers.
  - Hot shower or bath 60–90 minutes before bed to aid sleep onset.
  - Pre-sleep snack if needed: protein + complex carb (e.g., Greek yogurt with oats/berries) to stabilize blood sugar.
- Bedroom setup: dark (blackout curtains/eye mask), cool (17–19°C / 63–66°F), quiet (earplugs/white noise), comfortable mattress and pillow supporting neutral spine (pillow height keeps neck neutral).
- If you wake at night: stay dark/low light, 4–6 slow nasal breaths, brief bathroom break, back to bed; avoid phones.

Breathing and nervous-system downshift
- 90/90 or croc breathing: 4–6 minutes in the evening or post-training. Inhale 4–5 s through the nose, exhale 6–8 s, feel 360° rib expansion with light abdominal tension.
- Box breathing for pre-sleep: 4 s inhale, 4 s hold (soft), 6 s exhale, 2 s pause; 2–3 minutes.

Recovery habits across the week
- Movement snacks: every 45–60 minutes of desk time, stand for 2–3 minutes; do 5–8 reps each of hip hinge rock-backs, glute squeezes, scapular retractions, ankle pumps.
- Walking: 7,000–10,000 steps/day. Short 10–15 minute walk after meals to aid glucose control and inflammation.
- Hydration: bodyweight(kg) x 30–35 ml/day; add 500–750 ml around training. Include electrolytes on hot or high-sweat days.
- Anti-inflammatory nutrition: follow your plan; bias omega-3s and colorful produce on high-soreness days.
- Sunlight and nature time: 10–20 minutes outside daily for circadian rhythm and mood.
- Social and stress: brief 5–10 minute daily decompression (journaling, prayer, or gratitude list) to reduce stress load.

Spine-friendly recovery modalities
- Heat/contrast: warm shower or heat pack 10–15 minutes for stiffness; contrast shower (1–2 min cool, 2–3 min warm x 3–4 cycles) post-hard sessions if you enjoy it.
- Soft tissue: 5–8 minutes of light foam rolling for quads, adductors, glutes, T-spine. Avoid aggressive low-back rolling; if needed, use a peanut on T-spine only.
- Mobility: 8–12 minutes on non-lifting days: hip flexor half-kneeling stretch, adductor rock-backs, hamstring sliders, calf wall stretch, thoracic rotations, shoulder CARs.
- Light recovery cardio: 15–20 minutes Zone 1–2 (easy walk/bike) the day after heavy legs to reduce soreness.
- Sauna (optional): 1–3x/week, 10–20 minutes at tolerable temperature, rehydrate and add electrolytes afterward.
- Massage (optional): every 2–4 weeks; ask for focus on hips, glutes, T-spine; avoid deep lumbar pressure.

Supplements that support sleep/recovery
- Magnesium glycinate: 200–400 mg 60–90 minutes before bed.
- Glycine: 3–5 g before bed; may aid sleep depth and temperature regulation.
- Tart cherry concentrate: 1–2 tbsp diluted 60 minutes pre-bed may help soreness and sleep.
- Vitamin D3 per labs; fish oil and curcumin per your anti-inflammatory plan.
- Avoid stacking too many new aids at once; add 1 at a time for a week and assess.

Post-training cooldown template (8–10 minutes)
- 3–4 minutes easy cardio (bike/walk).
- Mobility: hip flexor stretch 30–45 s/side; adductor rock-backs 8 reps; T-spine open books 6/side.
- Breathing: 2–3 minutes 90/90 nasal breathing to switch off sympathetic drive.

Weekly recovery monitoring (2-minute check-in)
- Each morning: rate sleep quality (1–5), readiness (1–5), soreness (1–5), and stress (1–5). Note resting HR if you track it.
- Adjustments:
  - If two or more mornings show sleep ≤2 or readiness ≤2: reduce next session’s main-lift loads by 5–10% or drop 1–2 accessory sets.
  - If soreness ≥4 for two days, swap one cardio session to easy Zone 2 and focus on mobility/breathing.
  - If back tightness appears, remove any exercise that provokes it, shorten ROM, and prioritize core stability work that day.

Deload and peak week specifics (Week 8 and Week 12)
- Week 8: Prioritize 8–9 hours sleep, keep cardio Zone 2 only, add one extra breath/mobility session.
- Week 12 testing week:
  - Night before tests: 8+ hours sleep, stop fluids 60–90 minutes pre-bed to minimize awakenings.
  - Morning of: brief outdoor light, normal caffeine routine, no new supplements.
  - Between test days: easy 20-minute walk, light mobility, and 90/90 breathing; avoid deep tissue work.

Ergonomics for a desk worker
- Chair height: hips slightly higher than knees; feet flat; lumbar support maintaining neutral.
- Monitor: eye level; keyboard within elbows-at-90° reach; mouse close to body line.
- Microbreak alarm: every 50 minutes, stand and move.

- New or escalating back pain, radiating symptoms, or numbness/weakness.
- Sleep restricted to <6 hours for 2+ nights with high fatigue.
- Resting HR up >8–10 bpm above baseline for 2–3 days alongside poor readiness.

- No heavy spinal loading or loaded spinal flexion. Avoid back/front squats, heavy barbell deadlifts, good mornings, sit-ups/Crunch machines, heavy ab rollouts.
- Main implements: belt squat, goblet/DB, landmine, machines, hip thrusts, chest-supported rows, carries.

Week 12 (taper + testing)
- Test only on spine-sparing lifts. Keep all other work light (RPE 6) and volume -50–60%.
- Day 1 (Upper): Test DB bench 3RM. Ramp: 8 @ 40–50%, 5 @ 60%, 3 @ 70%, 2 @ 80%, 1 @ 85–90%, then 3RM; up to one more attempt +2–5%. Accessories: chest-supported row 3x5 @ RPE 7; Pallof 2x8/side.
- Day 3 (Lower—squat pattern): Test belt squat 1RM. Ramp: 5 @ 40–50%, 3 @ 60%, 2 @ 70%, 1 @ 80%, 1 @ 87–90%, 1 @ 93–95%, then 1RM; optional +2–3%. Back-off: 2x3 @ ~85%. Light delts/core after.
- Day 5/6 (Hinge): Test hip thrust 1RM (preferred) OR landmine RDL 3RM (safer than hinge 1RM). Use the provided ramping; back-offs 2x3 @ ~85% (hip thrust) or 2x3 @ ~90% (RDL 3RM).
- Cardio this week: Two easy Zone 2 sessions 20–25 min; no intervals within 48 h of lower-body tests.
- Safety: No grinders >RPE 9.5; perfect neutral spine; stop if any lumbar discomfort.

Anti-inflammatory nutrition (daily framework)
- Calories: maintenance to slight surplus (+0–10%) per goals.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day in 3–4 meals.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day, centered around training.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day emphasizing EVOO, avocado, nuts, omega-3s.
- Food priorities: fatty fish 2–3x/week; berries/cherries; leafy greens and crucifers; legumes/whole grains; herbs/spices (turmeric+pepper, ginger, garlic, cinnamon); fermented foods; green/oolong tea.
- Limit: added sugars, ultra-processed foods, processed meats, excess alcohol; identify personal triggers.
- Supplements: fish oil 1–2 g EPA+DHA; curcumin 500–1000 mg with meals (if cleared medically); vitamin D3 1000–2000 IU; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg; creatine 3–5 g/day; collagen 10–15 g + 50 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-lower-body sessions.
- Pre/post-workout: 25–40 g protein + 40–70 g carbs pre; 25–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbs post; hydrate with BW(kg) x 30–35 ml/day + 500–750 ml around training.

Sleep and recovery protocol
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night; consistent sleep/wake within ±30 min; cool (17–19°C), dark room; supportive pillow/mattress for neutral spine.
- Evening wind-down 60–75 minutes: dim lights/screens, light mobility (hips/T-spine), 90/90 or box breathing 4–6 min, hot shower 60–90 min pre-bed; optional tart cherry or glycine 3–5 g + magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg.
- Daytime: outdoor light AM and PM; caffeine cutoff ≥8 h before bed; alcohol cutoff ≥3–4 h; optional 10–20 min nap before 3 p.m.
- Recovery habits: 7,000–10,000 steps/day; microbreaks every 45–60 min at the desk; easy Zone 1–2 15–20 min the day after heavy legs; 5–8 min light foam rolling (avoid low-back) and mobility most days; sauna/massage optional.
- Monitoring: daily 1–5 scores for sleep, readiness, soreness, stress. If two metrics ≤2, reduce next session load 5–10% or drop 1–2 accessory sets; swap one cardio day to easy Zone 2 if sore.

Key substitutions if needed
- Belt squat: heavy goblet or 2-DB front squat; hack squat or leg press (comfortable ROM).
- Landmine RDL: DB RDL; cable pull-through.
- Chest-supported row: machine row/seal row.
- Hip thrust: DB hip thrust or floor glute bridge.
- Core: swap any drill that provokes symptoms for a simpler anti-rotation/anti-extension option.

Checkpoints
- End of Weeks 4 and 8: review technique tolerance, back status, and loads; adjust selections.
- Week 12: log 1RM/3RM results with ROM standards to guide the next block.

This plan builds general strength and work capacity while safeguarding the lumbar spine, adds targeted core and conditioning, and supports recovery with nutrition and sleep so he can push hard in Phase 2 and peak cleanly for Week 12 testing.
